how_this_was_validated.the_baseline_is_the_positive_control: A method that finds no object-scale error could be a method that cannot see one. The baseline variant of the same run carries a real 337-cell fabricated region and this analysis reports it at that size and shape, so the negative result on the candidate's missed-structure class is informative rather than an artifact of the instrument.
how_this_was_validated.the_guards_were_tested_by_corrupting_the: The guard suite is exercised against 11 mutations of this record in `harness/consumer_error_guard_mutations.py`, each applied to the real file and reverted. All are caught. The one worth reading is the first: the candidate's largest phantom component is exactly the frozen threshold, so moving the threshold to 9 would turn one structured component into none and make this record read better. One mutation found a real weakness rather than confirming a strength: a prose check that accepted the false sentence 'only 3 of the 79 components exceed 6 cells', because 3, 79 and 6 are all figures this record holds elsewhere. That check was replaced by regenerating the narrative from the measurements and comparing, which the same mutation then failed. Running the suite also surfaced two defects in the suite itself -- it ran pytest from the wrong directory, collected nothing, and scored every mutation as missed; and it restored the record with `git checkout`, which reverts to the last commit rather than to the bytes under test. Both were caught by its own assertions, which is the reason to write them.
how_this_was_validated.the_labeller_is_an_instrument_and_was_co: Component sizes are only meaningful if the labeller separates what it should. The control that matters is two blocks touching at a single corner: 26-connectivity reports one component, 6 reports two, and the run asserts both so the control cannot pass under the wrong setting. All 5 checks pass.
how_this_was_validated.the_reproduction_gate_came_first: The harness re-derives occupied, phantom and missed counts with the occupancy definition in `consumer_occupancy.py` and exits non-zero unless all six match `downstream-consumer.json`. They match, so the decomposition below describes the same cells the published record counts.

question: The mapping consumer's residual errors are reported as counts. Are they scattered single cells at the grid's resolution limit, or contiguous regions a consumer would be wrong about?

the_finding.the_error_class_that_would_actually_be_d: A phantom obstacle makes a planner conservative; a missed one makes it collide. So the missed-structure class is the one worth being afraid of, and on both variants it is sampling noise: 71 cells in 45 components on the baseline and 74 in 46 on the candidate, largest 7 cells with extent [1, 7, 1], and 0 components at or above the threshold on either. Every missed cell's nearest surface lies within 1.61 support radii (median 1.05), and 0 lie beyond five. These are cells whose mesh is right there, just outside the quantisation boundary -- not holes.
the_finding.the_recall_cost_of_the_crop_in_these_ter: The crop's recall cost is 3 cells. Both variants carry zero object-scale misses, so the cost is paid entirely in boundary cells, against 837 cells of structured fabrication removed.
the_finding.what_the_published_rate_hides: The published summary is a rate falling from 0.3245 to 0.0708. The rate is correct and it is not the interesting part. The baseline's fabrication is overwhelmingly coherent: 845 of its 871 phantom cells sit in 6 components of 8 cells or more, the largest 337 cells spanning [8, 15, 12] cells (0.337 m3 of invented solid). The crop does not thin that region out, it removes it.
the_finding.what_the_residual_error_is_instead: The candidate's 138 phantom cells are spread over 79 components, 52 of them single cells, with 8 cells in 1 component at or above the threshold. That component's extent is [1, 5, 2] cells -- 1 cell thick. A one-cell-thick sheet is what a distance-band occupancy test produces at the edge of a mesh that is in the right place, not a lump of geometry that is not there.

the_verdict.for_the_mapping_use: Fit for occupancy mapping at this cell size, with the residual error characterised rather than bounded away. The structured fabrication a consumer would be misled by falls from 845 cells to 8, and no missed-structure component on either variant is object-scale.
the_verdict.the_threshold_landed_exactly_on_the_boun: The threshold of 8 cells was frozen in the claim before any component size was known. The candidate's largest phantom component is 8 cells -- exactly the threshold -- so by the frozen gate the candidate does still carry one structured component, and this record says so rather than rounding it away. Moving the threshold to 9 would erase that sentence and is precisely the move the frozen gate exists to prevent. The shape reading is reported next to the size, not instead of it: that component is 1 cell thick where the baseline's largest is 8, so the two components the gate calls structured are not the same kind of error. A reader who wants one number should use the structured-cell count, not the component count.
the_verdict.what_this_does_not_say: Nothing here revisits collision fitness. `capability-record-collision-fitness.json` measured that separately and the verdict there stands: the surface is not closed, so inside/outside has no defined answer on it. Occupancy mapping is the narrower use that does not need closedness, which is why it is the use being assessed.

what_this_closes: `downstream-consumer.json` reports the mapping consumer's residual errors as counts: 138 phantom cells and 74 missed-structure cells on the cropped candidate. A count cannot separate the resolution limit of a 0.1 m grid from an unmapped wall, and those two readings would lead a mapping consumer to opposite conclusions. This record decomposes both error classes into 6-connected components and reports every component size and the largest component's shape.
